Reporting to the Director of Information Technology, you will help employees resolve hardware, software, account, and connectivity issues while supporting a Microsoft-based IT environment. This full-time, hourly position combines first- and second-level technical support with fieldwork and equipment inventory management. You will regularly travel to offices, treatment plants, and well sites throughout Arizona, including documenting the operational technology used at these facilities. The role requires in-person work in equipment rooms and plant environments, including outdoor conditions during Arizona summers, with compliance with site safety requirements. Key Responsibilities Provide first- and second-level technical support to employees in person, by phone, email, and remote support tools. Set up, configure, image, and deploy laptops, tablets, mobile devices, printers, and other peripherals. Create, manage, and troubleshoot user accounts, mailboxes, licenses, and access permissions. Support employee onboarding and offboarding, including account setup and removal, password-manager access, license assignments, and equipment preparation or recovery. Troubleshoot Microsoft 365 applications, Exchange Online email, and Microsoft Entra ID identity and sign-in issues. Diagnose basic wired, Wi-Fi, and VPN connectivity problems and escalate complex issues to the Director of Information Technology. Record, track, and resolve support requests through the ticketing system while keeping users informed of progress. Perform routine IT maintenance, including checking security patches and backups, reviewing system alerts, and maintaining phone and server equipment. Assist with software installations, patches, and updates across company devices. Maintain accurate records of IT hardware, software licenses, equipment assignments, and inventory. Label and tag equipment across company locations, coordinate warranty repairs, reconcile tracking records, and decommission retired hardware with verified data removal. Help maintain IT security practices, including multi-factor authentication, password policies, and phishing awareness. Travel regularly to offices, treatment plants, well sites, and other facilities across Arizona to provide on-site technical support. Support structured cabling, switches, wireless access points, workstation moves, and conference-room setups at the company's six offices. Visit plant and well sites to identify and document control systems, industrial controllers, radios, and monitoring devices as part of the operational technology inventory. Document procedures, troubleshooting solutions, and standard configurations for the IT knowledge base. Support other business systems and assist the Director of Information Technology with projects as assigned. Required Qualifications High school diploma or GED. At least one of the following: one year or more of hands-on IT support experience, CompTIA A+ certification, or an associate degree or technical certificate in an IT-related field. Basic understanding of Windows operating systems, desktop hardware, and common office software. Familiarity with Microsoft 365 and Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and Teams. Strong problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in helping users. Clear written and verbal communication skills. Ability to prioritize and manage multiple support requests in a fast-paced environment. Valid Arizona driver's license, a clean driving record, and the ability and willingness to travel to company facilities throughout the state. Ability to pass a pre-employment background check. Preferred Qualifications Experience or coursework with Microsoft business applications and administration, including Exchange Online, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Teams, and Intune. Exposure to Windows Server, cloud-hosted infrastructure, or basic networking concepts. Experience with enterprise firewalls; Fortinet exposure is a plus. Microsoft certifications such as MS-900 or AZ-900, or willingness to earn a certification. Experience supporting users across multiple physical locations. Experience with structured cabling, low-voltage systems, or field service. Interest in learning industry-specific systems, including SCADA and operational technology used in water and wastewater operations. JW Water offers on-the-job training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications and career development, along with the opportunity to work for a stable essential-services organization with a supportive team. Location and Work Arrangement This is a full-time, on-site position based in Phoenix, Arizona, with regular in-state travel to the company's six offices, treatment plants, well sites, and remote facilities. The role requires travel by company or personal vehicle and hands-on work in office and industrial environments. Physical requirements include lifting and moving IT equipment weighing up to 40 pounds, crawling under desks, reaching network and server equipment, and working in equipment rooms. Employees must follow site safety procedures and wear required personal protective equipment at treatment plants and well facilities, including when working outdoors in Arizona summer conditions.
